subject: An apothecary bench with brass scales, a scoop and dried plant material. The bench, mid morning.
A brass balance and a stack of weights on a stone bench. A balance and a set of weights. Everything worth knowing about a pot is a number, and every number can be checked.
Dried root, dried leaf and a curl of bark laid out on paper. Root, leaf and bark on paper. One plant, three products.
Empty capsule shells, halves separated, on a dark surface. Empty shells, halves apart. A capsule holds a fixed volume. Whatever is not plant is taking up room.
A stone mortar and pestle with milled plant material beside it. Mortar, pestle, milled material. Every pot is powder and a shell. The questions are which powder, how much, and what else went in.
An open notebook and pen beside a glass of water on a shop counter. Notebook, pen, glass of water. Four questions is usually enough. Write the answers down before you leave.
